title: Generative adversarial networks and how to evaluate generators
brief: Write the optimal discriminator and the Jensen-Shannon link, the saturating and non-saturating generator losses with their gradients, a matrix square root and the Frechet distance, and train a one-dimensional GAN.
hints: optimal_discriminator is p / (p + q), with 0.5 where p + q is 0. For N(0, 1) against N(2, 1) it equals sigmoid(2 - 2x), so D*(0) is about 0.8808 and D*(1) is exactly 0.5. js_divergence is 0.5 KL(p || m) + 0.5 KL(q || m) with m = (p + q) / 2, and it is 0.3368 for those two bells.

log(1 - sigmoid(b)) is -softplus(b), and log sigmoid(b) is -softplus(-b). Written that way, the losses stay finite at b = 800. The gradient with respect to b of log(1 - D) is -D, and of -log D it is D - 1. At b = -6, D is 0.00247, so the first is about -0.0025 and the second is about -0.9975, before dividing by the batch size.

Diagonalise: vals, vecs = eigh(A), clip vals at 0, and return (vecs * sqrt(vals)) @ vecs.T. frechet_distance is |mu1 - mu2|^2 + trace(S1) + trace(S2) - 2 trace(sqrtm_psd(R S2 R)), where R = sqrtm_psd(S1). Two identical Gaussians give 0 whatever their covariance. S1 = 4 I and S2 = 9 I in 3 dimensions give 3 (2 - 3)^2 = 3.

In train_gan_1d the discriminator loss gradient on features f = (x, x^2, 1) is mean(-(1 - D(real)) f_real) + mean(D(fake) f_fake). For the generator, the non-saturating gradient with respect to a fake sample x is (D(x) - 1) (w1 + 2 w2 x) / batch, and x depends on the generator through dx/da = z and dx/db = 1. Average (b, |a|) over the last 50 iterations.
